# mactf command-line reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_docs.py from `mactf help --format json`. Do not edit; run the script. -->

`mactf` is also `python -m mactf`, and a generated project's `manage.py` runs the same
commands. Global options are written after the command name, and after a subcommand name
when the command has one: `mactf runs list --format json` and `mactf runs --format json list`
are the same request. A global option before the command name is a usage error.

With `--format json`, `jsonl`, or `yaml`, standard output holds the payload and nothing
else; diagnostics, progress, and warnings go to standard error. The keys of a JSON payload
are only ever added to. Text layout is for people and may change between releases.

## Global options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--settings MODULE` | Settings module to load (default: the project found from the working directory). |
| `--pythonpath PATH` | Add a directory to sys.path; repeatable. |
| `--config FILE` | Overlay a YAML settings file above the environment; repeatable. |
| `--set KEY=VALUE` | Override one setting, for example TRAINING.EPOCHS=2; repeatable. |
| `--no-discover` | Do not look for a project; use the framework defaults. |
| `--format FORMAT` | text, json, jsonl, or yaml, where the command supports it. |
| `--json` | Same as --format json. |
| `-v / -q` | More / less output; -v may be repeated. |
| `--no-color / --force-color` | Colour is automatic; NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR are honoured. |
| `-y, --yes` | Answer yes to the confirmation of a destructive command. |
| `--traceback` | Show the Python stack instead of one error line. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OK` | Success. |
| 1 | `FAILURE` | The operation ran and the answer is no: a check failed, a checkpoint did not verify, a run failed, a plan is not applied. |
| 2 | `USAGE` | The invocation is wrong: bad arguments, unknown command, bad settings. |
| 3 | `NOT_FOUND` | A named run, episode, checkpoint, rule, peer, or settings key does not exist. |
| 4 | `CONFLICT` | It exists but its state forbids the action: the run is live, the id is taken, the file would be overwritten, the schema is behind. |
| 5 | `UNAVAILABLE` | The environment cannot do it: no QEMU, no IPython, the port is in use, an extra is missing. |
| 124 | `TIMEOUT` | `--timeout` elapsed. |
| 70 | `SOFTWARE` | A bug in mactf. Re-run with `--traceback` and report it. |
| 130 | `INTERRUPTED` | SIGINT or SIGTERM was honoured. |
| 141 | `PIPE` | The reader of stdout went away (`| head`). |

## `mactf redteam`

Run `run` with the stress pass forced on, then the injector pass. A failed injector is a
finding and makes the command exit 1.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--epochs EPOCHS` | Epochs to train before the injector pass (default 1). | `1` |
| `--peers PEERS` | Limit the number of peers. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Run the injectors against the untrained swarm. |  |
| `--injector {jailbreak_attempt,rogue_credit_thief}` | Run only this injector; repeatable. Repeatable. |  |
| `--list-injectors` | Print the injector catalog and exit; trains nothing. |  |
| `--device DEVICE` | auto, cpu, mps, cuda, or cuda:N. |  |
| `--seed SEED` |  |  |
| `--run-id RUN_ID` |  |  |
| `--timeout DURATION` |  |  |
| `--no-log` | Write no per-run log. |  |

```text
mactf redteam
mactf redteam --epochs 2 --injector jailbreak_attempt
mactf redteam --list-injectors --format json
```

## `mactf run`

Run the epoch loop. Progress prints one line per epoch. Ctrl-C once pauses the run at the
next epoch boundary so `--resume` can continue it; Ctrl-C twice aborts.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--epochs EPOCHS` | Total epochs (not additional epochs when resuming). |  |
| `--peers PEERS` | Limit the number of peers. |  |
| `--device DEVICE` | auto, cpu, mps, cuda, or cuda:N. |  |
| `--seed SEED` |  |  |
| `--redteam` | Force the stress pass on for this run. |  |
| `--no-redteam` | Force the stress pass off for this run. |  |
| `--task TASK` | Task source name, overriding TRAINING.TASK. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Build the swarm and record a dry_run row; train nothing. |  |
| `--resume [RUN]` | Continue a paused or interrupted run under its own id. |  |
| `--branch-from RUN[:EPISODE]` | Start a new run from a checkpoint of another run. |  |
| `--run-id RUN_ID` | Id for the run (default: generated). |  |
| `--timeout DURATION` | Wall-clock budget; the run pauses at the next epoch boundary (exit 124). |  |
| `--on-interrupt {pause,cancel}` | What Ctrl-C/SIGTERM makes of the run row. | `"pause"` |
| `--log-file PATH` | Write the per-run JSONL log here instead of the default location. |  |
| `--no-log` | Write no per-run log. |  |

Not allowed together: `--dry-run`, `--resume`, `--branch-from`.

Not allowed together: `--redteam`, `--no-redteam`.

Not allowed together: `--log-file`, `--no-log`.

```text
mactf run --epochs 3
mactf run --epochs 20 --timeout 2h --run-id nightly-01
mactf run --resume nightly-01 --epochs 40
mactf run --branch-from nightly-01:12 --epochs 30 --set COOPETITION.WEIGHT_CAP=0.5
mactf run --epochs 2 --format jsonl | jq -c 'select(.event == "epoch") | .score'
```

## `mactf checkpoints`

List, verify, roll back, and prune a run's checkpoints.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

### `mactf checkpoints list`

List a run's checkpoints.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |
| `--verify` | Hash and verify each file (reads every checkpoint). |  |
| `--valid-only` | Only checkpoints that verify; implies --verify. |  |
| `--best` | Only the *-best checkpoints. |  |

```text
mactf checkpoints list
mactf checkpoints list 9f3a --verify
```

### `mactf checkpoints show`

Describe and verify one checkpoint.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest'. |  |
| `episode` | Episode number or 'latest'. |  |

```text
mactf checkpoints show 9f3a latest
```

### `mactf checkpoints verify`

Verify checkpoint files; exit 1 if any fails.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest'. |  |
| `[episode]` | One episode; default: all. |  |

```text
mactf checkpoints verify latest
mactf checkpoints verify 9f3a 12
```

### `mactf checkpoints rollback`

Make an earlier checkpoint the newest one, so a resume continues from it.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest'. |  |
| `episode` | The episode to make newest. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Say what would happen; change nothing. |  |

```text
mactf checkpoints rollback 9f3a 12 --dry-run
```

### `mactf checkpoints prune`

Delete all but the newest checkpoints of a run.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id or unique prefix. |  |
| `--all` | Every run no process is driving. |  |
| `--keep KEEP` | Newest checkpoints to keep per run (default 3). | `3` |
| `--no-keep-best` | Do not protect *-best checkpoints. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Say what would be deleted; delete nothing. |  |

```text
mactf checkpoints prune 9f3a --keep 2
mactf checkpoints prune --all --dry-run
```

## `mactf inspect`

Inspect runs, episodes, rule counts, and checkpoints.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[target]` | Run id, or omit for the latest. |  |
| `--runs` | List recent runs. |  |
| `--episodes` | Include the episodes section. |  |
| `--rules` | Include the rules section. |  |
| `--checkpoints` | Include the checkpoints section. |  |
| `--warnings` | Include the warnings section. |  |
| `--adjudications` | Include the adjudications section. |  |
| `--aggregations` | Include the aggregations section. |  |
| `--resumes` | Include the resumes section. |  |

```text
mactf inspect
mactf inspect 9f3a --episodes --rules
mactf inspect --runs --json
```

## `mactf logs`

Read a run's JSONL log.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

### `mactf logs tail`

Print the last records of a run's log; --follow keeps printing new ones.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |
| `-n, --lines N` | Records to print (default 20). | `20` |
| `-f, --follow` | Keep printing records as they are written. |  |
| `--kind KIND` | run, epoch, step, loss, score, aggregation, warning, ... |  |
| `--level {debug,info,warning,error,critical}` | Only records of this level. |  |
| `--node NODE_PATH` | Only records of this node. |  |
| `--file PATH` | Read this JSONL file instead of a run's log. |  |

```text
mactf logs tail
mactf logs tail 9f3a -n 100 --kind epoch
mactf logs tail -f --level warning
mactf logs tail --format jsonl | jq .fields
```

### `mactf logs path`

Print where a run's log is (or would be).

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |

```text
tail -f $(mactf logs path)
```

## `mactf runs`

List, inspect, wait for, resume, cancel, and delete runs.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`, `yaml`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

### `mactf runs list`

List runs, newest first.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`, `yaml`; needs settings; aliases: `ls`.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--status STATUS` | A status, or active, resumable, final. Repeatable. Repeatable. |  |
| `--since WHEN` | Started at or after: 2h, 3d, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-01T08:30. |  |
| `--until WHEN` | Started at or before WHEN. |  |
| `--prefix PREFIX` | Only runs whose id starts with this. |  |
| `--limit LIMIT` | Rows to show (default 20). | `20` |
| `--all` | Every matching run. |  |
| `--reverse` | Oldest first. |  |

Not allowed together: `--limit`, `--all`.

```text
mactf runs list
mactf runs list --status failed --since 2d
mactf runs list --status active --format jsonl
```

### `mactf runs show`

Everything known about one run.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |
| `--episodes` | Include the episodes section. |  |
| `--rules` | Include the rules section. |  |
| `--checkpoints` | Include the checkpoints section. |  |
| `--warnings` | Include the warnings section. |  |
| `--adjudications` | Include the adjudications section. |  |
| `--aggregations` | Include the aggregations section. |  |
| `--resumes` | Include the resumes section. |  |
| `--all-sections` | Include every section. |  |

```text
mactf runs show
mactf runs show 9f3a --episodes --rules
```

### `mactf runs wait`

Block until a run stops being active.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |
| `--timeout DURATION` | Stop waiting after this long (exit 124). |  |
| `--interval DURATION` | Poll interval (default 2s). | `2.0` |

```text
mactf runs wait 9f3a --timeout 2h
```

### `mactf runs resume`

Continue a paused or interrupted run under its own id.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest' (the default). | `"latest"` |
| `--epochs EPOCHS` | Total epochs (not additional epochs). |  |
| `--device DEVICE` | auto, cpu, mps, cuda, or cuda:N. |  |
| `--timeout DURATION` | Wall-clock budget; pauses at the next epoch boundary (exit 124). |  |
| `--on-interrupt {pause,cancel}` | What Ctrl-C/SIGTERM makes of the run row. | `"pause"` |
| `--log-file PATH` | Write the per-run JSONL log here. |  |
| `--no-log` | Write no per-run log. |  |

Not allowed together: `--log-file`, `--no-log`.

```text
mactf runs resume
mactf runs resume nightly-01 --epochs 40
```

### `mactf runs cancel`

Mark a run nobody is driving as cancelled.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | Run id, a unique prefix of one, or 'latest'. |  |
| `--reason REASON` | Recorded in the run's notes. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Say what would happen; change nothing. |  |

```text
mactf runs cancel 9f3a --reason "bad seed"
```

### `mactf runs reap`

Mark active runs with no live process as interrupted.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | List the runs that would be reaped. |  |

```text
mactf runs reap --dry-run
mactf runs reap --yes
```

### `mactf runs delete`

Delete runs, their registry rows, checkpoints, and logs.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question; aliases: `rm`.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[run]` | Run ids or unique prefixes. |  |
| `--older-than DURATION` | Runs started more than this long ago. |  |
| `--status STATUS` | With --older-than: which statuses (default: final). Repeatable. |  |
| `--keep-files` | Delete rows only; leave checkpoint and log files. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Say what would be deleted; delete nothing. |  |

```text
mactf runs delete 9f3a --dry-run
mactf runs delete --older-than 30d --yes
```

## `mactf peers`

List the configured peers, describe a peer's contract, preview aggregation weights.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

### `mactf peers list`

List the configured peers.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings; aliases: `ls`.

```text
mactf peers list
```

### `mactf peers show`

Describe one peer and its input/output contract.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` |  |  |

```text
mactf peers show alpha
```

### `mactf peers contract`

Print only a peer's input/output contract.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` |  |  |

```text
mactf peers contract alpha
```

### `mactf peers weights`

What would the swarm's weights be for these scores? Changes nothing.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--score NAME=VALUE` | Repeatable. |  |
| `--eligible NAME=BOOL` | Default true for a peer not named. Repeatable. |  |
| `--confidence NAME=0..1` | Default 1.0 for a peer not named. Repeatable. |  |
| `--scores-file FILE` | JSON or YAML with scores/eligible/confidence (the API body); '-' reads standard input. |  |
| `--advance` | Step the throwaway temperature controller once. |  |

```text
mactf peers weights --score alpha=0.8 --score beta=0.6 --score gamma=0.2
mactf peers weights --scores-file scores.json --eligible gamma=false --format json
```

## `mactf rules`

List and explain the reward and penalty rules.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

### `mactf rules list`

List rules, filtered.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings; aliases: `ls`.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind {reward,penalty}` |  |  |
| `--tier TIER` | Repeatable. |  |
| `--severity SEVERITY` | Repeatable. |  |
| `--bucket {r_task,r_epi,r_collab,r_align,penalty}` |  |  |
| `--tag TAG` | Repeatable. |  |
| `--warning-eligible` | Only rules whose first S1 occurrence is a warning. |  |
| `--non-offsettable` | Only penalties no reward can offset. |  |
| `--omega` | Only rules that trigger the Omega amplifier. |  |
| `--search SEARCH` | Substring of id, name, or description. |  |
| `--sort {id,tier,severity,name}` |  | `"id"` |

```text
mactf rules list --kind penalty --severity major --severity severe
mactf rules list --tag honesty --format json
mactf rules list --non-offsettable
```

### `mactf rules show`

Describe one or more rules.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `RULE` | Rule ids such as R2 or P20 (case-insensitive). |  |

```text
mactf rules show P20 P21
mactf rules show r2 --format json
```

### `mactf rules tiers`

List the precedence tiers and the rules in each.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

```text
mactf rules tiers
```

### `mactf rules validate`

Check the catalog's own integrity; exit 1 if it is broken.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

```text
mactf rules validate
```

## `mactf check`

Run framework system checks (rules, scoring, peers, runtime, sandbox).

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--fail-level {ERROR,WARNING,INFO}` | The lowest level that makes the command fail. | `"ERROR"` |
| `--app APP` | Only this app's checks. |  |
| `--tag TAG` | Only checks carrying this tag; repeatable. Repeatable. |  |
| `--id PREFIX` | Only messages whose id starts with PREFIX (mactf.E0); repeatable. Repeatable. |  |
| `--list` | List the registered checks and exit; runs none. |  |

```text
mactf check
mactf check --fail-level WARNING
mactf check --app mactf.contrib.api --format json
mactf check --list
```

## `mactf config`

Show the effective settings and where each value came from.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

### `mactf config show`

Print the effective settings (or one table of them).

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[KEY]` | A dotted path such as TRAINING.EPOCHS. |  |
| `--origin` | Say which layer set each value. |  |
| `--changed` | Only values that differ from the framework defaults. |  |
| `--reveal` | Do not mask secrets. |  |

```text
mactf config show TRAINING
mactf config show --changed --origin
mactf --set TRAINING.EPOCHS=2 config show TRAINING.EPOCHS --origin
```

### `mactf config get`

Print one value, bare, for use in scripts.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `KEY` | A dotted path such as TRAINING.EPOCHS. |  |
| `--origin` | Print the originating layer after a tab. |  |
| `--reveal` | Do not mask secrets. |  |

```text
EPOCHS=$(mactf config get TRAINING.EPOCHS)
```

### `mactf config files`

List the layers settings were built from, lowest first.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

```text
mactf --config prod.yaml config files
```

### `mactf config validate`

Load and validate the settings; exit 2 if they do not load.

Formats: `text`, `json`, `yaml`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--strict` | Treat configuration notes as errors. |  |

```text
mactf --settings myproject.settings config validate
mactf --config overrides.yaml config validate --strict
```

## `mactf doctor`

Diagnose the environment: Python, torch, GPU, and sandbox isolation.

Formats: `text`, `json`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--require {cuda,qemu,hardware-isolation}` | Fail (exit 5) when this capability is missing. Repeatable. |  |

```text
mactf doctor
mactf doctor --format json
mactf doctor --require cuda --require qemu
```

## `mactf migrate`

Create or upgrade the run registry database.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--database PATH` | Override the sqlite path. |  |
| `--check` | Report only; exit 1 if the schema is behind or a migration is pending. |  |
| `--plan` | List pending migrations; apply none. |  |

Not allowed together: `--check`, `--plan`.

```text
mactf migrate
mactf migrate --check
mactf migrate --plan --format json
```

## `mactf sandbox`

Manage the QEMU hardware sandbox and inspect isolation capability.

Formats: `text`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--require {none,process,container,hardware}` | Exit 5 when the best usable isolation is below this level. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox
mactf sandbox --require hardware
mactf sandbox install --dry-run
mactf sandbox clean --dry-run
```

### `mactf sandbox status`

Probe every provider and report the best usable isolation.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--require {none,process,container,hardware}` | Exit 5 when the best usable isolation is below LEVEL. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox status
mactf sandbox status --require hardware
```

### `mactf sandbox install`

Install QEMU with the platform's package manager.

Formats: `text`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--force` | Run the installer even when QEMU is present. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Print the command without running it. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox install --dry-run
```

### `mactf sandbox provision`

Create the peer's overlay disk and spec.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--peer NAME` | Peer to build the spec for. | `"swarm"` |
| `--isolation {none,process,container,hardware}` | Isolation level; default is SANDBOX.ISOLATION. |  |
| `--no-fallback` | Refuse a weaker provider than requested. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox provision --peer alpha
mactf sandbox provision --isolation hardware
```

### `mactf sandbox launch`

Provision and start the peer's sandbox.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--peer NAME` | Peer to build the spec for. | `"swarm"` |
| `--isolation {none,process,container,hardware}` | Isolation level; default is SANDBOX.ISOLATION. |  |
| `--no-fallback` | Refuse a weaker provider than requested. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox launch --peer alpha
mactf sandbox launch --no-fallback
```

### `mactf sandbox clean`

Remove sandbox overlay disks and sockets.

Formats: `text`, `json`; needs settings; destructive: asks first; `--yes` skips the question.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | List what would be removed. |  |

```text
mactf sandbox clean --dry-run
```

## `mactf shell`

Open an interactive shell with settings and apps loaded.

Formats: `text`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--interface {auto,ipython,bpython,plain}` | Which interactive interpreter to use. | `"auto"` |
| `-c, --command CODE` | Execute CODE in the namespace and exit. |  |

```text
mactf shell
mactf shell -c "print(settings.database_path())"
mactf shell --interface plain < script.py
```

## `mactf serve`

Serve the MACTF API over HTTP (stdlib WSGI; use a production server for exposure).

Formats: `text`, `jsonl`; needs settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host HOST` | Address to bind (default HTTP.HOST). |  |
| `--port PORT` | Port to bind (default HTTP.PORT); 0 asks the OS for a free one. |  |
| `--workers WORKERS` | Process count; only 1 is supported. | `1` |
| `--verbose-access` | Print one line per request. |  |
| `--port-file PATH` | Write the bound port here once listening; removed on exit. |  |

```text
mactf serve
mactf serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000
mactf serve --port 0 --port-file .mactf-port --format jsonl
```

## `mactf startpeer`

Scaffold a new peer nn.Module inside an app directory.

Formats: `text`, `json`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Peer name, for example `critic_peer` or `peers/critic_peer`. |  |
| `--dir PATH` | Base directory; defaults to the project root. |  |
| `--state-dim N` | Input width of the generated module (default 16). | `16` |
| `--action-dim N` | Output width of the policy head (default 4). | `4` |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing file. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Print the path and class that would be written. |  |

```text
mactf startpeer critic_peer
mactf startpeer peers/critic_peer --state-dim 32 --dry-run
```

## `mactf startproject`

Scaffold a new MACTF project (settings, peers, configs, manage.py).

Formats: `text`, `json`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Project package name, for example `myswarm`. |  |
| `--dir PATH` | Parent directory; defaults to the working directory. |  |
| `--force` | Overwrite generated files that already exist. |  |
| `--dry-run` | List the files that would be written; write nothing. |  |

```text

mactf startproject myswarm --dir D:/work --dry-run
```

Print a tab-completion script for bash, zsh, fish, or PowerShell.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `shell` |  |  |
| `--prog NAME` | The program name to complete (default: mactf). | `"mactf"` |

## `mactf help`

Show the commands, or one command's options.

Formats: `text`, `json`; works without settings.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[COMMAND [SUBCOMMAND]]` | A command, optionally followed by one of its subcommands. |  |
| `--all` | List every subcommand under its command. |  |

```text
mactf help
```

## Deprecated

Nothing is deprecated.

## Appendix: the completion protocol

Shell completion scripts call back into the program with one process per Tab press:

```text
<program> __complete <shell> [--new-word] -- <word>...
```

The response is UTF-8, one line per item. The first line is always `:<directive>`; each
following line is `<value>` or `<value><TAB><description>`. The directive is a bit set:
`1` ask the shell for file names when there are no candidates, `2` do not append a space,
`4` ask the shell for directory names when there are no candidates. The scripts are
generated by `mactf completion <shell>`; nothing else is a supported caller.
